title: Completeness and residue calculation of a completed perfect coefficient model
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $I\subset A$ be a maximal ideal, and put $k=A/I$. On $T_{\mathrm{proét}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $B=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}\underline{A/I^n}$, using constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Let $P^\bullet$ be a bounded complex of finite projective $A$-modules, zero outside degrees $[a,b]$, and let $M^\bullet=B\otimes_A P^\bullet$ denote termwise extension of the constant complex; perfect complexes are [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Work in the module-sheaf derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Then $M^\bullet$ is locally derived $IB$-complete [def-weil-pbc-locally-derived-ringed-ideal-complete]. Its derived residue reduction [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] has the canonical isomorphism $M^\bullet\otimes^L_B\underline k\simeq\underline{P^\bullet\otimes_A k}$. For every integer $q$, its cohomology is the constant sheaf of the finite-dimensional $k$-vector space $H^q(P^\bullet\otimes_A k)$, and both $M^\bullet$ and its residue reduction have zero cohomology outside $[a,b]$. The same assertions hold on every covering slice, with the restricted coefficient sheaf. No finiteness of the set $k$, no regularity of $A$, and no perfectness of $A/I^n$ over $A$ is required.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11, reverse implication; proetale.tex Tag 099Q (proposition-enough-weakly-contractibles); sites-modules.tex Tags 093M (lemma-completion-flat), 093J (lemma-constant-exact); sites-cohomology.tex Tag 06YS (lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat).

proof.text:
For each nonzero term $P^i$, choose generators and the resulting surjection $s_i:A^{r_i}\to P^i$. Projectivity lifts $\mathrm{id}_{P^i}$ to $u_i:P^i\to A^{r_i}$ with $s_i u_i=1$. Thus $e_i=u_i s_i$ is an idempotent matrix and $P^i\cong\operatorname{im}(e_i)$. Constant sheaves preserve these splitting equations and finite sums: for finite sums this follows by applying exactness to split short exact sequences. Tensoring with $B$ gives $M^i\cong\operatorname{im}(e_i:B^{r_i}\to B^{r_i})$. Limits of module sheaves are sectionwise. For every section object, a compatible family in the images of the reductions of $e_i$ is exactly a compatible family $x_n$ satisfying $e_i x_n=x_n$; this is equivalent to $e_i(\lim x_n)=\lim x_n$. Consequently the quotient projections induce a canonical isomorphism
$$M^i\cong\varprojlim_{n\geq1}\underline{P^i/I^nP^i}.$$
Here the level-$n$ image is $P^i/I^nP^i$ because the original splitting reduces modulo $I^n$. This argument is termwise and assumes no compatibility of chosen splittings with the differentials.

source.place: Tag 093J (lemma-constant-exact); finite-projective direct-summand calculation applied to the completion limit

proof.text: The Noetherian hypothesis makes $I$ finitely generated. Each sheaf $\underline{P^i/I^nP^i}$ is killed by $I^n$. Apply the torsion-limit completeness theorem to the inverse-limit presentation in step 1: the bounded complex $M^\bullet$, regarded as a complex of $\underline A$-modules, is locally derived $I\underline A$-complete. Its hypotheses allow an arbitrary scheme $T$, arbitrary transition maps, and infinite underlying residue sets. Restriction of scalars along $\underline A\to B$ preserves and reflects local derived completeness for the extended ideal. Apply that theorem to this $B$-complex and the ideal $I\underline A$. It follows that $M^\bullet$ is locally derived $IB$-complete, with exactly the internal-Hom-on-every-slice convention in the statement.

The canonical map from the constant ring to its completion has $B/IB\cong\underline{A/I}=\underline k$, by the quotient clause of the constant-completion theorem, with the quotient induced by the first projection. Use this identification for the $B$-action on $\underline k$. The coefficient theorem applies to every ideal of every commutative Noetherian $A$; it requires neither regularity nor a finite underlying quotient set.

For a $B$-module sheaf $F$, tensor with $M^i$ is the image of the idempotent $e_i$ acting on $F^{r_i}$. This is an exact functor: for an exact sequence, kernels are computed in the ambient finite direct sums, and a section in the target image lifts locally to some $x$ and hence to $e_i x$ in the source image. Thus every $M^i$ is flat over $B$. Since the complex is zero above $b$, the bounded-above-flat theorem makes $M^\bullet$ K-flat. Derived change of rings along $B\to\underline k$ is therefore computed by the ordinary complex $M^\bullet\otimes_B\underline k$.

source.place: Tag 06YQ (lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat); derived change of rings computed on K-flat complexes

proof.text:
In each degree the canonical tensor map sends $(b\otimes p)\otimes c$ to $\overline b\,c\otimes\overline p$ in $\underline{P^i\otimes_A k}$. It is an isomorphism for $P^i=A^{r_i}$ by step 3 and the tensor unit, and for $P^i$ by applying the splitting $u_i,s_i$ on both sides. Its inverse is the restriction of the inverse on those free modules to the images of the same idempotent. The formula is balanced over $A$ and $B$ and is natural in every $A$-linear map $P^i\to P^{i+1}$: both orders send $(b\otimes p)\otimes c$ to $\overline b\,c\otimes\overline{d^i p}$. Hence these maps form the canonical chain isomorphism
$$M^\bullet\otimes_B^L\underline k\simeq\underline{P^\bullet\otimes_A k}.$$
No resolution of $k$ or of $A/I^n$ by finite projectives has been used.

Write $C^\bullet=P^\bullet\otimes_A k$. Exactness of the constant-sheaf functor identifies the kernel of $\underline{d^q}$ with $\underline{\ker d^q}$ and the image of $\underline{d^{q-1}}$ with $\underline{\operatorname{im}d^{q-1}}$, and then identifies their quotient with $\underline{H^q(C^\bullet)}$. Each $C^q$ is a direct summand of $k^{r_q}$, so it is finite-dimensional. Its kernel and the quotient of that kernel by the image of the preceding differential are finite-dimensional $k$-vector spaces. This proves the asserted constant finite residue cohomology. Outside $[a,b]$ both $M^\bullet$ and $C^\bullet$ have zero terms, hence zero cohomology. If $a>b$ all terms are zero and the same argument applies.

source.place: Tag 093J (lemma-constant-exact), applied to cycles, boundaries and their quotient

proof.text: Let $U\to T$ be any covering object, or indeed any object of $T_{\mathrm{proét}}$. Weakly etale localization identifies $T_{\mathrm{proét}}/U$ with $U_{\mathrm{proét}}$ and identifies restricted constant ring sheaves with the corresponding constants on $U$. Sectionwise limits then identify $B|_U$ with $\varprojlim_n\underline{A/I^n}_U$, using the same projections. Restriction is exact, preserves K-flat complexes, and commutes with ordinary sheaf tensor. Thus the restricted complex is $(B|_U)\otimes_A P^\bullet$ and its derived residue is the restriction of the chain isomorphism in step 5; exactness identifies its cohomology with restriction of that in step 6. Apply steps 1–2 on the scheme $U$ to obtain completeness with respect to $I(B|_U)$. All their hypotheses still hold, since no hypothesis on $T$ beyond being a scheme was used. This proves every assertion on every covering slice with the restricted coefficient sheaf.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q134-e6ead4840 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item. The 7-step split creates no new node and keeps the statement and stmt_deps unchanged. It matches the reverse direction of Bhatt–Scholze Prop 6.6.11 (via Lemma 6.5.8 and the residue of the constant model). Step checks: (1) a finite projective P^i is the image of an idempotent e_i, so M^i ≅ lim (P^i/I^n P^i)_T by sectionwise limits and exact constant sheaves. (2) lem-weil-pbc-torsion-limit-sheaf-completeness covers bounded complexes of such limits, and lem-weil-pbc-restriction-local-completeness (an iff with no hypotheses; its JB is the item's IB) gives locally derived IB-complete. (3) The quotient clause of the constant-completion equivalence at n=1 gives B/IB = k. (4) Summands of B^r are flat, the complex is bounded above so it is K-flat, and derived change of rings is computed on K-flat complexes, so no Tor hypothesis is needed. (5) The chain isomorphism holds degreewise through e_i and is natural in d. (6) The constant functor is exact and each term is a summand of k^r, so the cohomology is finite-dimensional and vanishes outside [a,b]. (7) Weakly étale localization, restriction commuting with tensor, and restriction preserving K-flat complexes give the slice case. Stacks tags 093J, 093M, 06YQ, 0E8K, 03EL, 099Q and 099C were checked in the tag table. Edge cases checked: Z_(p); k[e]/e^2 with I=(e); a field with I=0; the zero complex; an infinite residue field. The statement gives exactly what parent lem-sfb-adic-stratified-perfect uses in its steps 4 and 5. The nine generic module-sheaf tool_uses are accepted. Live and side-live still have the item unsplit. Maintainer note: the item's source.place, and also lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site, cite Tag 06YS for lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat; the correct tag is 06YQ. Both are maintainer-owned fields, so I did not fix them.
